metadata.description: Comprehensive information about horse coat colors, patterns, and markings

base_colors.name: Bay
base_colors.description: Brown body with black points (mane, tail, lower legs, ear edges)

genetics.genetic_basis: Genetically a black horse (E) with the agouti gene (A) that restricts black pigment to the points
genetics.inheritance: Agouti (A) is dominant to non-agouti (a). Requires at least one dominant Extension (E) allele
genetics.notation: E_A_ (where _ indicates either dominant or recessive allele can be present)

variants.name: Light bay
variants.description: Yellow-tan to light brown body with black points

variants.name: Blood bay
variants.description: Rich, reddish brown body with black points

variants.name: Dark bay
variants.description: Dark brown body with black points, can be mistaken for black

variants.name: Mahogany bay
variants.description: Very dark reddish-brown, nearly brown body with black points

variants.name: Wild bay
variants.description: Bay with minimal black on the legs, often only on fetlocks
variants.genetic_note: Caused by a different form of the agouti gene (A+)

base_colors.historical_significance: One of the most common and historically favored colors for cavalry and working horses
base_colors.identification_tips: Look for the sharp demarcation between the body color and black points. Dark bays require close inspection of the flanks or muzzle in sunlight to distinguish from true black

base_colors.name: Black
base_colors.description: True black coat with no brown areas, may sunbleach to brownish in some horses

genetics.genetic_basis: Produced by the dominant Extension gene (E) without the Agouti (A) gene that would restrict black pigment
genetics.inheritance: Requires at least one dominant Extension (E) allele and two recessive agouti (a) alleles

variants.name: Faded black
variants.description: Black that appears brownish due to sun exposure or nutritional factors
variants.note: Not a genetic variation but an environmental effect

variants.name: True black
variants.description: Deep, non-fading black with no brown tones

variants.name: Coal black
variants.description: Intense black with bluish highlights, particularly glossy

base_colors.historical_significance: Traditionally favored for funeral horses, formal occasions, and by some military units
base_colors.identification_tips: True blacks have black skin and dark eyes. Check muzzle, flanks, and around eyes in bright sunlight for any brownish tint that would indicate a very dark bay instead of true black
base_colors.care_notes: More susceptible to heat absorption in hot climates; may sunbleach requiring special grooming products to maintain color

base_colors.name: Chestnut
base_colors.description: Reddish-brown coat with mane and tail the same color as body or lighter (flaxen), no black points

genetics.genetic_basis: Caused by the recessive extension gene (e), which prevents black pigment expression
genetics.inheritance: Requires two recessive extension alleles (e); agouti gene has no visible effect
genetics.notation: ee (A_ or aa, agouti status irrelevant)

variants.name: Sorrel
variants.description: Light, coppery red shade of chestnut, commonly used term in Western breeds
variants.note: Often used interchangeably with chestnut in some regions and breeds

variants.name: Liver chestnut
variants.description: Dark, purplish or chocolate brown shade of chestnut

variants.name: Light chestnut
variants.description: Pale reddish or golden shade of chestnut

variants.name: Flaxen chestnut
variants.description: Any shade of chestnut with distinctly lighter mane and tail
variants.genetic_note: Flaxen trait is separately inherited and not fully understood genetically

base_colors.historical_significance: The most widespread color in some ancient breeding traditions; Suffolk Punch draft horses are exclusively chestnut
base_colors.identification_tips: No black hairs anywhere on the body; even the darkest chestnuts have reddish, not black, manes and tails. Legs are the same color as the body or slightly darker but never true black

base_colors.name: Gray
base_colors.description: Born dark and progressively lightens with age, often developing dapples during the graying process

genetics.genetic_basis: Caused by the dominant Gray gene (G) that causes progressive depigmentation of the hair
genetics.inheritance: Dominant trait - only one copy needed to cause graying; acts on any base color
genetics.notation: G_ (single dominant gene regardless of other color genes)
genetics.progression: All gray horses are born a different color (black, bay, chestnut, etc.) and gray with age

variants.name: Steel gray
variants.description: Early stage of graying with mixture of colored and white hairs, giving a steely appearance
variants.age_relation: Usually younger horses in early graying stages

variants.name: Dapple gray
variants.description: Gray with distinct circular patterns of lighter and darker hairs
variants.age_relation: Middle stage of graying process, highly prized pattern

variants.name: Fleabitten gray
variants.description: Nearly white coat with small, red or black flecks throughout
variants.genetic_note: Caused by small areas of resistant pigment cells
variants.age_relation: Usually appears in older gray horses after initial graying

variants.name: White gray
variants.description: Final stage where horse appears completely white, though skin remains dark
variants.age_relation: Usually older horses in final graying stage

variants.name: Rose gray
variants.description: Gray process acting on a chestnut base, giving a pinkish or rosy appearance
variants.age_relation: Early to middle stage of graying on chestnut base

base_colors.historical_significance: Traditionally favored for military officers' mounts and parade horses; Lipizzaners are born dark and selected for their ability to turn pure white
base_colors.health_considerations: Gray horses have higher incidence of melanoma, especially under the tail and around the anus, eyes, and genitals
base_colors.identification_tips: Gray horses always have dark skin (except under white markings), dark eyes, and are born a darker color. Check the muzzle - if skin is pink, it's white, not gray

base_colors.name: Palomino
base_colors.description: Golden coat with white or flaxen mane and tail

genetics.genetic_basis: Chestnut base (ee) with one cream dilution gene (CCr)
genetics.inheritance: Requires two recessive extension alleles (ee) and one cream gene (CCr)
genetics.note: Breeding two palominos has 25% chance of cremello, 50% palomino, 25% chestnut

variants.name: Golden palomino
variants.description: Ideal golden color similar to a newly minted gold coin

variants.name: Light palomino
variants.description: Lighter cream to white-gold color, sometimes called isabela in some countries

variants.name: Chocolate palomino
variants.description: Darker, bronze or chocolate shade with flaxen mane and tail
variants.note: Sometimes confused with silver dapple on black base

variants.name: Pearl palomino
variants.description: Palomino with pearl gene giving a metallic sheen
variants.genetic_note: Pearl is a separate dilution gene with subtle effects

base_colors.shade_variations: Palomino can range from light cream (almost approaching cremello) to deep, rich gold
base_colors.historical_significance: Highly prized in Spanish colonial traditions; popularized in America through film and television with horses like Roy Rogers' Trigger
base_colors.registration_requirements: Some color breed registries require specific shade ranges and minimal dark skin for palomino registration
base_colors.identification_tips: True palominos have dark skin (except under white markings) and dark eyes. Main body color should be distinctly golden, not cream or white

base_colors.name: Buckskin
base_colors.description: Tan or gold body with black points (mane, tail, lower legs)

genetics.genetic_basis: Bay base (E_A_) with one cream dilution gene (CCr)
genetics.inheritance: Requires dominant extension (E), dominant agouti (A), and one cream gene (CCr)

variants.name: Golden buckskin
variants.description: Clear golden body color with distinct black points

variants.name: Sooty buckskin
variants.description: Buckskin with sooty or smutty overlay darkening portions of the coat
variants.genetic_note: Sooty factor is not well understood genetically

variants.name: Silvery buckskin
variants.description: Lighter, silvery-tan shade of buckskin

variants.name: Buttermilk buckskin
variants.description: Pale creamy-yellow buckskin, lighter than typical

base_colors.historical_significance: Traditional color of many cavalry mounts and war horses; valued in Western riding traditions
base_colors.distinguishing_from_dun: Often confused with dun, but buckskins lack the primitive markings (dorsal stripe, leg barring) unless they also carry the dun gene

base_colors.name: Dun
base_colors.description: Tan body with primitive markings (dorsal stripe, leg barring, shoulder stripe)

genetics.genetic_basis: Caused by the dun dilution gene (D) which dilutes the body color but leaves the primitive markings
genetics.inheritance: Dominant trait - one copy produces full dun effect
genetics.notation: D_ (can act on any base color)

primitive_markings.name: Dorsal stripe
primitive_markings.description: Dark line running down the spine from mane to tail

primitive_markings.name: Leg barring
primitive_markings.description: Horizontal dark stripes on the legs, particularly visible on the forearms

primitive_markings.name: Shoulder stripe
primitive_markings.description: Dark transverse stripe across the withers/shoulders, sometimes called a cross

primitive_markings.name: Ear tips
primitive_markings.description: Dark edging or tips on the ears

primitive_markings.name: Cobwebbing
primitive_markings.description: Dark lines on the forehead, also called spider marks

variants.name: Red dun
variants.description: Dun dilution on a chestnut base; produces yellowish or reddish body with red primitive markings

variants.name: Yellow dun (classic dun)
variants.description: Dun dilution on a bay base; produces tan body with black primitive markings

variants.name: Grullo/Grulla
variants.description: Dun dilution on a black base; produces smoky or mouse-colored body with black primitive markings

variants.name: Dunalino
variants.description: Dun and cream dilutions on a chestnut base; palomino with dun markings

variants.name: Dunskin
variants.description: Dun and cream dilutions on a bay base; buckskin with dun markings

base_colors.historical_significance: One of the oldest equine colors; wild horse populations typically display dun coloration with primitive markings for camouflage
base_colors.identification_tips: Always look for the dorsal stripe and other primitive markings; dun dilutes the body color but leaves points and primitive markings dark

base_colors.name: Roan
base_colors.description: Mixture of white hairs evenly intermingled with base color hairs throughout the body, head and legs typically remain solid

genetics.genetic_basis: Caused by the dominant Roan gene (Rn)
genetics.inheritance: Simple dominant, though there is evidence of lethality in homozygous form in some lines
genetics.notation: Rn_ (can appear on any base color)
genetics.note: True roan is present at birth and doesn't change with age (unlike gray)

variants.name: Blue roan
variants.description: Roan pattern on black base coat, giving a blue-gray appearance

variants.name: Red roan
variants.description: Roan pattern on chestnut base coat, giving a strawberry or pinkish appearance

variants.name: Bay roan
variants.description: Roan pattern on bay base coat, bay points remain dark

variants.name: Strawberry roan
variants.description: Term sometimes used interchangeably with red roan, or for a lighter variant

identifying_characteristics: White hairs don't increase with age
More prominent in summer coat, may appear darker in winter coat
Often shows 'corn marks' (solid spots) from previous injuries where white hairs don't grow
base_colors.distinguishing_from_gray: Roans keep their pattern throughout life and are born roaned; grays progressively lighten and are born a solid color

base_colors.name: Cream
base_colors.description: Creamy coat with pink skin and blue eyes, results from double cream dilution

genetics.genetic_basis: Caused by two cream dilution genes (CCrCCr) acting on base colors
genetics.inheritance: Must inherit one cream gene from each parent

variants.name: Cremello
variants.description: Double cream dilution on chestnut base; cream-colored coat with pink skin and blue eyes

variants.name: Perlino
variants.description: Double cream dilution on bay base; slightly darker cream with reddish points, pink skin, blue eyes

variants.name: Smoky cream
variants.description: Double cream dilution on black base; smoky cream color with pink skin and blue eyes

base_colors.historical_significance: Often called 'white horses' historically, though they are genetically different from true white
base_colors.health_considerations: Pink skin requires sun protection; blue eyes may be more sensitive to bright light
base_colors.identification_tips: All double dilutes have pink skin and blue or bluish-green eyes, distinguishing them from white horses with dark skin and dark eyes

base_colors.name: Champagne
base_colors.description: Dilution that lightens coat color and produces golden body tones with mottled skin and amber eyes

genetics.genetic_basis: Caused by the dominant Champagne gene (CH)
genetics.inheritance: Dominant trait - one copy produces full champagne effect
genetics.notation: CH_ (can act on any base color)

characteristics: Mottled skin, especially around eyes, muzzle and genitals
Amber or hazel eyes, often changing from blue at birth
Lightened coat with metallic sheen
Light-colored hooves

variants.name: Classic Champagne
variants.description: Champagne on chestnut base; gold coat with similar mane and tail

variants.name: Amber Champagne
variants.description: Champagne on bay base; tan body with chocolate points

variants.name: Sable Champagne
variants.description: Champagne on black base; chocolate to taupe color

variants.name: Gold Champagne
variants.description: Another term sometimes used for classic champagne

base_colors.distinguishing_characteristics: Mottled skin is the definitive characteristic of champagne; often confused with palomino or buckskin but has different skin and eye color
base_colors.foal_characteristics: Born with pink skin and blue eyes that change to mottled skin and amber eyes with maturity

patterns.name: Tobiano
patterns.description: White pattern that typically crosses the topline between withers and tail, with white legs and sharply defined vertical edges

genetics.genetic_basis: Caused by the dominant Tobiano gene (TO)
genetics.inheritance: Simple dominant - one copy produces pattern

characteristics: White crossing the back between withers and tail
Regular, oval-shaped markings with vertical orientation
Four white legs common
Head usually dark with normal facial markings
Sharp, distinct borders between colors
Tail often bicolored

variants.name: Minimal tobiano
variants.description: Minimal white, often just crossing the topline and white on legs

variants.name: Classic tobiano
variants.description: Roughly equal amounts of white and base color

variants.name: Medicine hat
variants.description: Mostly white with color just on the ears and poll area, chest and flank shield
variants.historical_note: Considered sacred by some Native American tribes

patterns.distinguishing_from_overo: Tobiano consistently has white crossing the topline and has smooth, oval-shaped markings with clean edges

patterns.name: Overo
patterns.description: A collective term for several genetically distinct white spotting patterns that typically don't cross the topline, with irregular edges and face markings

subcategories.name: Frame Overo
subcategories.description: White patterning appears to be 'framed' by color around the edges of the body

genetics.genetic_basis: Caused by the Lethal White Overo gene (O)
genetics.inheritance: Heterozygous (O/o) produces pattern, homozygous (O/O) fatal - produces lethal white foal syndrome

characteristics: White does not usually cross the topline
White usually centered on body with colored 'frame' around edges
At least one and often all four legs are dark
Bold white head markings common, often blue eyes
Jagged, horizontally oriented edges to white patches
subcategories.health_considerations: Breeding two frame overos has 25% chance of lethal white foal syndrome (OLWS)

subcategories.name: Splashed White
subcategories.description: Looks like the horse has been dipped in white paint from below, with white on the legs and face

genetics.genetic_basis: Several different mutations can cause splashed white patterns
genetics.inheritance: Dominant with variable expression
genetics.chromosome: Located on several different chromosomes depending on variant

characteristics: White begins at the underside and 'splashes' upward
Bottom-heavy pattern with legs, belly, and lower body white
White face, often with blue eyes
Relatively crisp edges to white areas

subcategories.name: Sabino
subcategories.description: White spotting with roaned edges, often with white extending up the legs and face

genetics.genetic_basis: Complex pattern with multiple genetic factors, one identified as Sabino-1 (SB1)
genetics.inheritance: Sabino-1 is dominant; homozygous produces more white
genetics.notation: SB1_ (but many sabino-patterned horses don't carry SB1)

characteristics: White extending up legs (high stockings or socks)
White belly spots common
Roaned or 'lacy' edges at borders of white areas
White chin spots and blaze common
Sometimes includes flecks or roaning throughout coat

patterns.distinguishing_from_tobiano: Overo patterns typically don't cross the topline, have irregular edges, and include bold face white

patterns.name: Appaloosa
patterns.description: Complex spotting pattern with several distinctive characteristics and variants

genetics.genetic_basis: Complex pattern involving the Leopard Complex gene (LP) and pattern genes (PATN)
genetics.inheritance: LP is incomplete dominant; pattern genes modify expression
genetics.chromosome: Leopard Complex is on equine chromosome 1

identifying_characteristics.name: Mottled skin
identifying_characteristics.description: Pink and black speckled skin, particularly around muzzle, eyes, genitals

identifying_characteristics.name: White sclera
identifying_characteristics.description: Visible white around the eyes (most horses have dark sclera)

identifying_characteristics.name: Striped hooves
identifying_characteristics.description: Vertical dark and light stripes on hooves, even on solid-colored legs

identifying_characteristics.name: Sparse mane and tail
identifying_characteristics.description: Thinner, shorter hair in mane and tail compared to other breeds

variants.name: Leopard
variants.description: White body with colored spots distributed over entire body

variants.name: Blanket
variants.description: White patch over hips/loin area, often with spots within the white

variations.name: Blanket with spots
variations.description: White blanket with colored spots within it

variations.name: Blanket without spots
variations.description: Solid white blanket over hips

variants.name: Snowflake
variants.description: Dark body with white flecks or small spots scattered throughout

variants.name: Frost
variants.description: Scattered white hairs intermixed with base color, similar to roan but not uniform

variants.name: Varnish roan
variants.description: Progressive roaning that spreads across body while leaving dark 'varnish marks' on bony prominences
variants.age_factors: Often becomes more pronounced with age

variants.name: Few spot leopard
variants.description: Almost entirely white with minimal colored spots, often just on knees, hocks, and base of ears
variants.genetic_note: Typically homozygous LP/LP with specific pattern genes

patterns.historical_significance: Developed by the Nez Perce tribe for its camouflage value and distinctive appearance
patterns.age_related_changes: Many Appaloosa patterns change with age, often showing more white or visible roaning

patterns.name: Brindle
patterns.description: Uncommon pattern of vertical or slightly slanted stripes of varying colors

genetics.genetic_basis: Multiple possible causes, including chimerism, somatic mutation, and the rare dominant Brindle 1 (BR1) gene
genetics.inheritance: Varies depending on cause; true genetic brindle is dominant
genetics.notation: BR1_ for genetic brindle; other types have different origins
genetics.rarity: One of the rarest color patterns in horses

variants.name: True (genetic) brindle
variants.description: Heritable pattern of vertical stripes on body

variants.name: Chimeric brindle
variants.description: Stripes caused by two embryos fusing in early development, creating mixed cellular populations

variants.name: Somatic mutation brindle
variants.description: Stripes caused by mutations occurring during embryonic development

common_breeds: Slightly more common in Quarter Horses and Mustangs
historical_examples: Dunbars Gold (Quarter Horse stallion, likely BR1 carrier)
Reindeer (historical British brindle horse documented in 1800s)

patterns.name: Dominant White
patterns.description: Pattern producing white coat with underlying pink skin, caused by several different mutations

genetics.genetic_basis: Multiple forms of the dominant white gene (W), numbered W1 through W27+
genetics.inheritance: Dominant, some variants may be lethal in homozygous form
genetics.notation: W1_, W2_, etc. (each family has its own mutation)
genetics.chromosome: Located on equine chromosome 3, KIT gene

characteristics: Pink skin under white hair (unlike gray horses, which have dark skin)
Dark eyes (usually)
Born white and remains white throughout life
Variable expression - can range from completely white to having colored patches

variants.name: W1 (Purebred White Arabian)
variants.description: Original dominant white variant discovered in Arabians

variants.name: W2 (Camarillo White)
variants.description: Variant found in Camarillo White Horses

variants.name: W5 (Thoroughbred white)
variants.description: White thoroughbred variant stemming from the mare White Beauty

variants.name: W10 (Standardbred white)
variants.description: Variant found in Standardbred pedigrees

variants.name: W20 (Quarter Horse white)
variants.description: White variant found in certain Quarter Horse lines

patterns.progression: Born white and stays white, unlike gray which is born dark and lightens progressively
common_breeds: Found in various breeds as separate mutations
patterns.distinguishing_from_other_white_patterns: Complete or near-complete white with pink skin from birth, typically dark eyes

variations.name: Small star
variations.description: Small, distinct white patch

variations.name: Irregular star
variations.description: Asymmetrical or oddly shaped white mark

variations.name: Faint star
variations.description: Star with scattered white hairs rather than solid white

face_markings.name: Stripe
face_markings.description: Narrow white marking running down the face

variations.name: Narrow stripe
variations.description: Thin, defined line down the face

variations.name: Broad stripe
variations.description: Wider stripe, but not as wide as a blaze

variations.name: Interrupted stripe
variations.description: Stripe that breaks or narrows at some point

face_markings.name: Blaze
face_markings.description: Wide white marking running down the face

variations.name: Full blaze
variations.description: Wide marking extending from forehead to muzzle

variations.name: Irregular blaze
variations.description: Blaze with uneven edges or varying width

variations.name: Tapered blaze
variations.description: Blaze that narrows as it extends down the face

face_markings.name: Snip
face_markings.description: White mark between or on the nostrils

variations.name: Small snip
variations.description: Small spot between nostrils

variations.name: Large snip
variations.description: Larger white area covering much of muzzle

variations.name: Connected snip
variations.description: Snip that connects to a stripe or blaze

face_markings.name: Bald Face
face_markings.description: Extensive white face that extends beyond the eyes and to the sides

variations.name: Full bald face
variations.description: White covering entire face from forehead to muzzle and extending beyond eyes

variations.name: Apron face
variations.description: Extremely extensive white covering face and jawbones

face_markings.name: Combination markings
face_markings.description: Combinations of the basic face markings

examples.name: Star and stripe
examples.description: Distinct star connected to a stripe

examples.name: Interrupted blaze
examples.description: Blaze with a break in the middle showing base coat color

leg_markings.name: Coronet
leg_markings.description: White just above the hoof, extending no more than an inch above the hoof

variations.name: Regular coronet
variations.description: Even band just above the hoof

variations.name: Irregular coronet
variations.description: Uneven white band around coronary band

variations.name: Partial coronet
variations.description: White marking on only part of the coronary band

leg_markings.name: Pastern
leg_markings.description: White extending from hoof to pastern joint
leg_markings.height_reference: Extends above coronet but stops below fetlock joint

variations.name: Low pastern
variations.description: White extends just above coronet

variations.name: High pastern
variations.description: White extends to just below fetlock

leg_markings.name: Sock
leg_markings.description: White extending from hoof to fetlock joint
leg_markings.height_reference: Extends up to the fetlock joint but not above it

variations.name: Short sock
variations.description: White barely reaches fetlock

variations.name: Full sock
variations.description: White completely covers fetlock area

leg_markings.name: Stocking
leg_markings.description: White extending from hoof well above fetlock, may reach knee or hock
leg_markings.height_reference: Extends above fetlock, potentially to knee/hock or higher

variations.name: Half stocking
variations.description: White extends midway between fetlock and knee/hock

variations.name: Full stocking
variations.description: White reaches or passes knee/hock

variations.name: Extended stocking
variations.description: White extends above knee/hock onto upper leg

leg_markings.name: Irregular markings
leg_markings.description: Leg markings with irregular edges or patterns

examples.name: Ermine marks
examples.description: Small black spots within white markings

examples.name: Bordered markings
examples.description: White leg markings with colored border

examples.name: Lightning marks
examples.description: Jagged streaks of white extending up dark leg

body_markings.name: Dorsal Stripe
body_markings.description: Dark line running along the spine from mane to tail
body_markings.genetic_association: Common feature of dun dilution, but can appear faintly in other colors

width_variations.name: Broad
width_variations.description: Wider than standard, sometimes with indistinct edges

body_markings.name: Zebra Markings
body_markings.description: Horizontal stripes on legs, also called leg barring
body_markings.genetic_association: Feature of dun dilution, more visible on front legs

variations.name: Bold barring
variations.description: Distinct, clearly visible stripes

variations.name: Faint barring
variations.description: Subtle, sometimes barely visible stripes

variations.name: Partial barring
variations.description: Stripes visible on only part of the leg

body_markings.name: Bider Marks
body_markings.description: Dark marks across the withers, perpendicular to dorsal stripe
body_markings.genetic_association: Feature of dun dilution, also called shoulder stripe or cross

body_markings.name: Cobwebbing
body_markings.description: Fine, net-like dark markings on the face
body_markings.genetic_association: Feature often seen with dun dilution
body_markings.location: Typically on forehead or frontal area

body_markings.name: Bend Or Spots
body_markings.description: Small, scattered dark spots on base coat, usually on barrel or quarters
body_markings.named_after: Thoroughbred stallion Bend Or who exhibited these spots
body_markings.genetic_basis: Likely somatic mutations affecting pigmentation during development
body_markings.inheritance: Not heritable in the traditional sense

body_markings.name: Whorls
body_markings.description: Circular hair growth patterns where hair grows in different directions

significance.identification: Used as identifying characteristics similar to fingerprints
significance.behavioral_correlations: Some research suggests correlation between whorl position and temperament

rare_colors.name: Silver Dapple
rare_colors.description: Dilutes black pigment in mane, tail and body, often with dappling

genetics.genetic_basis: Caused by the dominant Silver gene (Z)
genetics.inheritance: Dominant, affects only black pigment (black and bay base colors)
genetics.effect: Dilutes black pigment but has no effect on red pigment

appearance_on_base_colors.effect: Body becomes chocolate to pale silver-gray, mane and tail typically lighter silver-white
appearance_on_base_colors.name: Silver black (also called Silver, Silver Dapple, or Chocolate)

appearance_on_base_colors.effect: Body becomes lighter red-brown, mane and tail silver-white
appearance_on_base_colors.name: Silver bay (also called Red Silver or Chestnut Silver)

appearance_on_base_colors.effect: No visible effect as there is no black pigment to dilute
appearance_on_base_colors.name: Visually chestnut (but may carry and pass on silver gene)

rare_colors.health_considerations: Associated with Multiple Congenital Ocular Anomalies (MCOA) syndrome, particularly in homozygous form
rare_colors.distinguishing_characteristics: Lighter mane and tail than body (opposite of flaxen chestnut); typically shows dappling on body

rare_colors.name: Champagne
rare_colors.description: Dilutes both red and black pigment, creates metallic sheen and mottled skin

genetics.genetic_basis: Caused by the dominant Champagne gene (CH)
genetics.inheritance: Dominant - one copy produces full champagne effect

characteristics: Mottled skin, especially visible around eyes, muzzle, and genitals
Amber or hazel eyes (blue at birth)
Metallic sheen to coat
Dilutes both red and black pigments
Pink skin that often develops 'freckles' with sun exposure

variants.effect: Gold body with gold or slightly lighter mane and tail
variants.name: Gold Champagne

variants.effect: Chocolate to taupe-colored body and points
variants.name: Classic Champagne (or Sable)

combinations.description: Very diluted coat with characteristic champagne skin and eyes
combinations.names: Various depending on base color (e.g., Gold Ivory, Amber Cream, etc.)

combinations.description: Diluted coat with primitive markings and champagne characteristics
combinations.names: Various depending on base color (e.g., Gold Dun, Amber Dun, etc.)

rare_colors.distinguishing_from_similar_colors: Often confused with palomino or buckskin, but mottled skin and amber eyes are distinctive champagne traits

rare_colors.name: Pearl
rare_colors.description: Subtle dilution that enhances red pigment, double effect when paired with cream gene

genetics.genetic_basis: Caused by the Pearl gene (prl), a mutation in the MATP gene
genetics.inheritance: Recessive - one copy has subtle effect, two copies produce visible dilution

appearance.on_chestnut: Subtle brightening of coat color, skin slightly lighter
Similar to cremello but with darker skin, amber eyes instead of blue
appearance.on_bay: Pale coat with slightly darker points, skin not as pink as double cream
appearance.on_black: Uniformly diluted coat, similar to smoky cream but with amber eyes

appearance.description: Called 'pseudo-double dilute' - similar to double cream dilutes but with amber/green eyes

rare_colors.historical_context: Long present in Iberian breeds but only identified genetically in the 21st century
rare_colors.distinguishing_characteristics: Subtle shell-like iridescence to coat, often with amber or green-tinted eyes

rare_colors.name: Mushroom
rare_colors.description: New dilution identified in 2013, creates lilac-like color with chocolate and diluted tones

genetics.genetic_basis: Recessive mutation in the MFSD12 gene
genetics.inheritance: Recessive - two copies needed for expression

appearance.effect: Pale golden taupe with pinkish tones

rare_colors.rarity: Extremely rare, still being documented and studied
rare_colors.distinguishing_characteristics: Unique lavender-taupe tint to coat unlike other dilutions

rare_colors.name: Pangare (Mealy)
rare_colors.description: Light coloration on soft areas like muzzle, eyes, flanks, belly, and inner legs

genetics.genetic_basis: Not fully understood, likely polygenic
genetics.inheritance: Unclear, appears to be dominant with variable expression

appearance.effect: Lighter tan around soft areas, particularly visible on muzzle and flanks
Lighter brownish areas around muzzle and soft areas
Very light, almost cream colored soft areas

rare_colors.historical_significance: Characteristic of primitive horse types and ancient breeds
rare_colors.intensity_variations: Ranges from subtle to very pronounced lightening of soft areas

color_combinations.name: Bay Tobiano
color_combinations.description: Bay base coat with tobiano pattern

genetics.inheritance: Requires dominant extension (E), dominant agouti (A), and dominant Tobiano (TO)

variations.description: Light bay with minimal tobiano
Dark bay with extensive tobiano

color_combinations.name: Palomino with Flaxen
color_combinations.description: Golden coat with very light, almost white mane and tail

genetics.inheritance: Palomino (chestnut with cream gene) plus flaxen factors

color_combinations.distinguishing_from_regular_palomino: Flaxen palominos have a more pronounced difference between body and mane/tail color

color_combinations.name: Blue Roan Appaloosa
color_combinations.description: Blue roan base with appaloosa spotting pattern

genetics.inheritance: Requires black base (E_aa), dominant roan (Rn), and leopard complex (LP)

color_combinations.characteristics: Unique combination of roaning throughout body with appaloosa characteristics (mottled skin, spotted blanket, etc.)

color_combinations.name: Buckskin Tobiano
color_combinations.description: Buckskin base coat with tobiano pattern

genetics.inheritance: Buckskin (bay with cream) plus tobiano

variations.description: Golden buckskin with minimal tobiano
Light buckskin with extensive tobiano

color_combinations.name: Silver Bay Dapple
color_combinations.description: Bay with silver dilution causing chocolate body and silvery mane and tail

genetics.inheritance: Bay base with silver dilution gene

color_combinations.dappling_characteristics: Silver often causes pronounced dappling in the coat
color_combinations.health_concerns: May be associated with Multiple Congenital Ocular Anomalies (MCOA)

color_combinations.name: Black Splash White
color_combinations.description: Black base coat with splash white pattern

genetics.inheritance: Black base with any splash white gene variant

color_combinations.characteristics: Black with distinct white patches typically on the lower parts of the body and face

color_combinations.name: Cremello Tobiano
color_combinations.description: Cremello base (double cream dilution of chestnut) with tobiano pattern

genetics.inheritance: Cremello base with tobiano gene

color_combinations.appearance: Very light cream colored with pink skin, blue eyes, and patches of slightly darker cream or white
color_combinations.pattern_visibility: Often subtle due to minimal contrast, most visible when wet or in certain lighting

color_combinations.name: Grullo Appaloosa
color_combinations.description: Grullo base (dun on black) with appaloosa patterns

genetics.inheritance: Black base with dun dilution and leopard complex

color_combinations.distinguishing_characteristics: Mouse-colored body with primitive dun markings and appaloosa characteristics (blanket, leopard spots, etc.)

progression.description: Born any base color (black, bay, chestnut, etc.)
White hairs begin appearing around eyes and muzzle, often within first year
progression.timeframe: Usually begins before 2 years of age

progression.description: Increasing mixture of white and colored hairs, often creating dappled appearance
Mostly white with some colored hairs remaining
Completely or almost completely white, sometimes with fleabitten specks
progression.timeframe: 8-15 years typically, though some horses never become completely white

variations.name: Slow graying
variations.description: Some gray horses gray very slowly, retaining much original color into their teens

variations.name: Fast graying
variations.description: Some gray rapidly, appearing almost white by age 4-5

progression.description: Born with some roaning visible, but not full adult pattern
Roaning becomes more pronounced after first foal shed
Roaning often more prominent in summer coat, less visible in winter coat
May be born with minimal pattern or different pattern than adult coat
Patterns like varnish roan, blanket, or leopard spots often develop or change with age
progression.timeframe: Progressive changes through first few years

progression.description: Appaloosa roaning (especially varnish roan) often increases with age
Mottled skin, striped hooves, white sclera become more pronounced with maturity

variations.name: Few Spot progression
variations.description: Some spotted foals eventually develop into few spot leopards with minimal spots

variations.name: Snowflake progression
variations.description: White flecks often increase in number and size with age

progression.description: Often born mousy-gray or reddish without clear black points
Black points (legs, mane, tail) develop and darken
Full bay coloration with clear black points established

Used in many American breed registries
